The Chinese vessels included four fishing boats, which engaged in “simultaneous operations’ that the coastguard described as “hybrid warfare”.
Taiwan’s coastguard said its vessels took “forceful action immediately to effectively neutralise the threats” and accused Beijing of “attempting to unilaterally alter the status quo” in the Taiwan Strait and give the “false impression of jurisdiction”.
Some of the vessels reportedly entered Taiwan’s restricted waters.
Beijing claims Taiwan and Pratas as part of its territory and asserts jurisdiction over the surrounding waters, which Taipei rejects. China has long threatened to use force to regain control of Taiwan.
In an incident on October 1 , Taiwan’s coastguard fired water cannon at a Chinese recreational fishing vessel near Pratas island between Taiwan and mainland China that Beijing claims.
China has intensified its maritime pressure on Taiwan in recent months. Beijing deployed a record 244 coastguard, scientific research and other ships around Taiwan’s main island in July, Taiwanese official data show, compared with just 58 in the same month last year.
In the first 21 days of August, 152 vessels were detected; most were from the Chinese Coastguard, but fishing boats and research vessels were also involved.
China also deploys warships around Taiwan on a near-daily basis, but those are counted separately.

Shabana Mahmood to hold talks with EU over law enforcement cooperation
UK home secretary’s meeting comes after PM said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases
The UK home secretary, Shabana Mahmood , will meet the EU’s home affairs commissioner on Monday for further talks just days after Andy Burnham said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases from which the UK has been locked out of since Brexit.
According to the European Commission , they will discuss “migration, border management, law enforcement cooperation and counter-terrorism”, with the latest Frontex data published on Monday showing a 43% decline in small boats crossing the Channel.
It will be the second time Mahmood has met Magnus Brunner in two months and comes amid an increase in engagement between London and Brussels since Andy Burnham announced he would use an upcoming EU-UK summit to “ lay out to the country ” what he believes are the “different options for Britain’s long-term relationship” with the EU.
Brexit’s back – but are British voters ready to contemplate a reversal?
Brunner said “the UK’s contribution is indispensable” to continuing efforts to suppress irregular migration after the EU introduced a suite of new laws aimed at speeding up asylum decisions and deportations.
On the agenda for Monday’s meeting will be talks on the UK rejoining some of the police and security databases it was locked out from after Brexit and rejoining a new database, Eurodac , centring on migration.
Last week Burnham told MPs that “one of the most positive aspects of my meeting with [the European Commission] president [Ursula] von der Leyen in New York, was her openness to the conversation about restoring data sharing on immigration across the UK, across Europe”.
He said it was “control” that the UK “lost” and should get “more attention” in the debate about Brexit . “I will work hard to see if we can get a practical arrangement on that very issue at the summit in November,” Burnham said.
Magnus Brunner will discuss ‘migration, border management, law enforcement cooperation and counter-terrorism’ with Shabana Mahmood, according to the European Commission. Photograph: Dursun Aydemir/Anadolu/Getty Images Brunner will also meet the MI5 director general, Ken McCallum, and visit the National Counter Terrorism Security Office, as well as meet senior officials from the UK’s child sexual abuse centre to discuss joint efforts to tackle such crimes.
He has also been chosen to deliver a lecture at King’s College London on migration and asylum, where he will talk about the impact of the EU’s new Pact on Migration and Asylum, a framework of 10 pieces of legislation overhauling how the EU manages its borders, processes asylum applications and shares information among member states.
Brunner will tell those he meets that the new laws have already had a significant impact along with a shift in political priorities around migration in key countries such as Germany, Italy and France.
He said the “reforms are paying” off in the UK too, with illegal crossings down 43%.
“We must stay on this course, including along all relevant migration routes, and the UK’s contribution is indispensable,” he said. “We have put our European house in order. Illegal crossings at our external borders are down 55% over two years, with a further third this year, and asylum applications are at record lows in the countries that used to be main destinations.”
One key database the UK wants access to is Eurodac, a new platform which collects fingerprints and facial images of asylum seekers from the age of six, and security flags for people linked to terrorism or serious crime.
Another is the Schengen Information System (SIS), which contains data on missing persons, stolen goods, vehicles and number plates, and fugitives crossing internal EU borders. About 20m searches are made daily on the SIS, according to EU data, mostly on cars.

Trump defends decision to waive some sanctions on Russia; Lithuania foils attack on Starlink site; Kyiv hits another oil terminal. What we know on day 1,699
Donald Trump has defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, while once again accusing Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. “My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” the US president wrote on Truth Social. “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him … he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did,” he added. Trump’s remarks come after he signed an executive order on Friday putting on hold a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy.
Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskyy had thanked the Trump administration for resuming intelligence sharing between the two countries , but maintained the US had intentionally throttled its Starlink satellite internet access to send a “message” to Kyiv, write Andrew Roth and Sam Jones.
Lithuania said Russia was likely behind an attempted arson attack on a company hosting communication hardware for Starlink satellites . Prime minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius made the claim on broadcaster LRT after authorities discovered flammable liquids at the company in question. Sinkevicius said the firm, whose location he did not mention, houses “nine satellite antennas to guarantee the Starlink connection, which of course supports and assists Ukraine”. He added: “It is obvious this is part of the hybrid war being waged by Russia, involving acts of sabotage.”
In September, a satellite station belonging to the network located in central Poland was set ablaze with Warsaw claiming sabotage. In Bulgaria, an investigation is under way amid claims that antennas linked to the Starlink satellite network were set on fire .
Shipping Russian diesel to the US market will take 15 to 20 days once contracts are signed , a senior Russian official said on Sunday, though a date for signing has yet to be announced. Trump announced the controversial agreement with Moscow last week, seen as a way to try to lower fuel prices for American consumers ahead of crucial midterm elections. “Negotiations are currently under way regarding the commercial terms – that is, on finalisation of the contracts,” Russian deputy prime minister for energy Alexander Novak said in an interview with state media. “Once the contracts are signed, the fuel will reach the markets – in this case, the US markets – within 15 to 20 days.”

A logistics centre belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a datacentre operated by Russian tech company VK were also targeted, the companies confirmed. Iran's foreign minister accuses Netanyahu of pushing US toward another war to avoid prison
Iran's foreign minister accuses Netanyahu of pushing US toward another war to avoid prison
Abbas Araghchi warns Tehran has ‘unfinished jobs’ of its own as Trump endorses Israeli leader ahead of elections
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu late Sunday of seeking to drag the United States into another war with Iran to avoid imprisonment while warning Washington against renewed military action.
“Netanyahu is driving America into another war to stay out of jail,” Araghchi wrote on the US social media platform X, accusing the Israeli leader of disregarding the consequences for Israel and US President Donald Trump.
“Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job,’ Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful; we have unfinished jobs too,” he added.
His remarks came after Trump endorsed Netanyahu earlier Sunday ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 elections, praising their partnership in confronting Iran and warning that Washington might have to take on the task itself if Israelis elected another leader.
“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using Netanyahu’s nickname.
Netanyahu has headed the current government since late 2022, which has been described as the most right-wing in Israel’s history. He is also standing trial domestically on corruption charges that could carry prison sentences if convicted and has been wanted by the International Court of Justice since 2024 for war crimes in Gaza.
Opposition parties have intensified coordination in an effort to replace Netanyahu’s government through the ballot box.
The US and Israel launched military strikes against Iran on Feb. 28, prompting retaliatory attacks by Tehran.
Despite an April ceasefire and a framework agreement reached in June, fighting later resumed as negotiations between Washington and Tehran stalled.

items.summary: Putin suggests meeting with Trump, Xi to discuss Ukraine war resolution - report  The Jerusalem Post
items.content:
Putin suggests meeting with Trump, Xi to discuss Ukraine war resolution - report
This comes as Trump and Zelensky publicly criticize the other's decisions, with Trump claiming that Zelensky 'doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did.'
Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a meeting with Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff at the Kremlin in Moscow, Russia, September 5, 2026.
( photo credit : SPUTNIK/GAVRIIL GRIGOROV/POOL VIA REUTERS )
Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed a meeting with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping next month to discuss ending the Russia-Ukraine war, the Wall Street Journal reported Sunday night, citing people familiar with the discussions.
The talks would not involve Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky , an unprecedented move which would be expected to alarm many European countries, WSJ wrote.
According to the report, the Kremlin suggested the three leaders meet on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which takes place Nov. 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, southern China.
Putin first suggested the meeting while speaking to Trump on October 9, in the same conversation in which the two leaders agreed that the US would buy Russian diesel fuel and facilitate its sale, a former Russian intelligence officer told WSJ .
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed that discussions over a potential meeting were ongoing.
US PRESIDENT Donald Trump with Chinese President Xi Jinping after a visit to the Zhongnanhai Garden in Beijing, May 15. (credit: Evan Vucci/Pool/File/Reuters)
“There is no clear understanding yet regarding the meeting itself or its potential agenda, although all three parties acknowledge the hypothetical possibility of such a meeting taking place,” he told WSJ .
A senior US official told WSJ that Trump hadn't agreed to the meeting but may be receptive to the idea due to his desire to end the war.
Trump, Zelensky clash over Ukrainian attacks, US sanctions
This comes as Trump and Zelensky publicly criticize the other's decisions, with Zelensky saying on Saturday that Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia and tariffs on its goods days before they were to take effect will embolden Moscow to keep attacking Ukraine, and Trump suggesting that Ukraine needs a new president.
Trump claimed that Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did," in a post on Truth Social earlier on Sunday, calling on the Ukrainian leader to stop attacking Russian diesel refineries.
Neither the White House nor the Chinese Embassy in Washington has commented on the report, but analysts told WSJ that a meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin could advance Xi's ambitions for China's place in global diplomacy.
“China wants to be seen as the pivot of the great powers, and potentially as a mediator between the US and Russia,” Yun Sun, director of the China program at the Stimson Center, a Washington think tank, told WSJ .
However, Chinese officials have expressed concern that the meeting could overshadow China's role in the region at APEC, according to the report.
People familiar with the discussions told WSJ that Xi is also trying to balance support for Putin and economic ties with Europe. A meeting with Putin and Trump to discuss Ukraine could raise the risk of European backlash.

Goldman Sachs sees S&P 500 earnings at $415 in 2027 but warns narrow leadership is a risk
Goldman Sachs expects US stocks to keep rising on earnings growth but warns narrow market leadership, near its tightest since the dot-com era, leaves momentum trades vulnerable. It sees S&P 500 EPS at $415 in 2027 and favours lagging consumer stocks.
Goldman’s view supports staying invested in US equities, but it points to rotation rather than broad gains. The recent slide in the momentum factor suggests that rotation may already be under way, with crowded AI and mega-cap trades most exposed. Oil is a key swing factor: elevated crude prices tied to the Iran war are part of what restrains growth in Goldman’s base case, so any further energy shock would delay the consumer recovery it is banking on for 2027. Rate-sensitive and lower-income consumer names stand to benefit most if inflation and yields ease. Third-quarter earnings over the coming weeks will test whether profit forecasts hold up.
Only a third of the US data centre pipeline looks credible as AI financing strains build
Goldman still sees room for US stocks to climb, but with the index propped up by a narrow group of winners, it is telling investors to look for the next leaders rather than chase the last ones.

Goldman’s momentum factor fell 8% in one week, highlighting the risk to crowded trades
Goldman forecasts S&P 500 EPS of $375 in 2026 and $415 in 2027, with its 2028 estimate about 7% below consensus
AI capex accounts for about half of S&P 500 earnings growth, a boost expected to fade
Goldman favours lagging consumer stocks, particularly those tied to lower-income households and experiences, on expected real income gains in 2027
Goldman Sachs expects the US stock market rally to continue on the back of rising corporate profits, but its equity strategists warn that unusually narrow market leadership leaves investors who chase recent winners exposed to a sharp reversal.
In a report dated 16 October, a team led by strategist Ben Snider argued that slowing economic and earnings growth should moderate equity returns rather than bring the advance to an end. Their preferred opportunity lies in consumer stocks that have lagged the market, which they expect to benefit from improving household purchasing power next year.
The concern sits beneath the headline index. When the report was written, the S&P 500 was only about 2% below its record high, yet the typical stock in the index was around 15% below its own peak. Goldman’s measure of market breadth was close to its narrowest since the dot-com era. That gap is a risk for momentum strategies, which favour recent outperformers: either lagging stocks catch up, or the leaders fall back toward the pack, and both outcomes would hurt trades built on the previous leadership. Goldman’s momentum factor dropped 8% in a single week, showing how quickly those positions can unwind.
Earnings remain the main support. Goldman forecasts S&P 500 earnings per share of $375 in 2026 and $415 in 2027. Stripping out one-off accounting effects, it puts underlying growth at around 29% this year and 18% next. But the bank sees less room for the large upward revisions that have powered stocks, and its 2028 estimate of $460 a share sits roughly 7% below consensus.
Artificial intelligence is central to that outlook. Goldman estimates AI capital spending accounts for about half of S&P 500 earnings growth, a contribution it expects to fade as spending growth slows and depreciation costs rise. That view sits alongside other recent signals on the AI buildout, from forecasts showing memory costs swallowing a growing share of hyperscaler budgets to reports of data centre projects stalling on grid power constraints.
Higher interest rates and oil prices are also expected to weigh on activity. Goldman’s consumer thesis rests on those pressures easing in 2027, with lower inflation, energy prices and rates lifting real incomes, particularly for lower-income households. It forecasts real income growth for the bottom fifth of earners accelerating from 0.4% in 2026 to 1.8% in 2027. Hedge fund exposure to consumer discretionary stocks is near multiyear lows, which could amplify any recovery, though Goldman is selective, favouring lower-income consumer names and experience-related businesses rather than the sector as a whole.
Historically, periods of positive but slowing growth have still delivered gains, driven by earnings rather than rising valuations, and have favoured companies with durable growth and lower volatility. The risk is a deeper slowdown. With cyclical stocks already losing ground to defensives, the path for the market’s recent leaders looks harder from here.

items.title: Better AI Chip Stock: Taiwan Semiconductor vs. Micron - The Motley Fool
items.summary: Better AI Chip Stock: Taiwan Semiconductor vs. Micron  The Motley Fool
items.content:
While companies like Nvidia and  AMD may get most of the headline glory in the AI realm for their powerful processors, the reality is these companies only design some of the chips that go into data centers. The fabrication muscle in the sector lies in a handful of chip foundry businesses, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM -2.28% ) and Micron ( MU -5.63% ) being the two largest in the world by market cap.
But which one makes for the better buy? Let's dig in, as these two are very different investments.
Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor aren't competitors
On the surface, Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor are both chip foundry companies. Both take in client orders, then create their chips. However, that's where the similarities end.
Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor produce two entirely different types of chips; Micron designs and makes memory chips, and Taiwan Semiconductor makes logic chips designed by other companies. Both are required in accelerated computing units like GPUs, but each serves a different role.
Furthermore, the technologies behind each one are radically different. There isn't a ton that separates one memory chip from another. Take basic computer RAM, for example. Nobody cares a lot about which brand of RAM is in a laptop, only what capacity that RAM has. That's because most memory chips are practically the same, although Micron is challenging that notion. It recently agreed to design an industry-first custom memory chip for Nvidia's GPUs, which could be a different avenue to lock in better long-term contract deals.

Because one manufacturer's memory chips are much like another's, they are subject to commodity-like pricing. This year, demand for memory chips has steeply outpaced supply, causing prices to soar. The shortage is expected to get worse in 2027 and 2028, which would allow Micron to keep turning huge profits on its chips.
The logic chips that come out of Taiwan Semiconductor's foundries are completely different. Companies like Nvidia and AMD design processors, and their various devices can deliver competitive edges on a range of criteria as the chipmakers work to improve speed, energy efficiency, transistor density, and more. Choosing a reliable chip manufacturer is a big part of this design process, and with TSMC's massive production facilities, proven track record, and leading technology, it's the partner that is most often selected. However, TSMC has relatively greater production capacity than the memory chip industry, and has been expanding production capacity in recent years, so it was able to mostly handle the AI demand rush.

Micron holds an edge in the revenue growth department, as it's still benefiting from the effect of soaring memory chip prices due to the shortage. However, TSMC's growth rate isn't bad either.
TSM Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.
Another area where Micron holds an edge is valuation. Investors today can pick up Micron shares at a much cheaper 5.3 times forward earnings compared to TSMC's 24.
Why the huge price discrepancy? It all has to do with Micron operating in what has historically been a highly cyclical industry. Every time memory demand outpaces supply, the chipmakers start to build new fabs. By the time they come online, the demand waves have often slackened, supply leaps ahead, and prices tumble.
The market isn't convinced that the current wave of intense memory chip demand driven by the AI infrastructure build-out will last, and it's discounting it as a result. But Micron and others in the memory industry have said the shortage is going to get worse before it gets better. If Micron's stock rises throughout the year due to strong demand, it could deliver incredible returns.
TSMC is also a solid investment, and because the logic chip industry is not as cyclical (it still is, but not to the same degree), the market is not as concerned about its outlook, and therefore is not valuing the stock at a discount.
I think this is a huge mismatch, and Micron makes for the better buy, at least when upside potential is considered. While TSMC is still a fantastic investment, the mismatch between Micron's stock price and its earnings potential is just too much to ignore. Investors should pounce on the deal.

items.title: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
items.summary: Prime Minister Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".
items.content:
By Jessica Murphy ,Â  Canada digital editor Â  and Â  Nadine Yousif ,Â  Senior Canada reporter ,Â  Reporting from Edmonton
Four members of the Canadian military have died and dozens were injured in a major fire at a base in the province of Alberta.
Addressing the nation on Sunday from Ottawa, Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime".
The fire broke out at about 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases, and is now contained. Its cause is still unclear, but officials said it did not appear tied to "terrorist activity".
"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces who we have lost," said Carney.
The BBC has confirmed that Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark have died.
Of the 39 injured people being cared for in hospital, at least 19 are in a critical condition, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said at a press briefing on Sunday evening.
Fire and rescue teams are remaining at the scene to contain any potential flare-ups, Wainwright Mayor Bruce Pugh told the BBC.
Members of the infantry had been conducting "high-intensity combat training with live munitions" at a grenade range and attack range, where 10 soldiers practise attacking a simulated enemy, Maj-Gen Wade Rutland told reporters at the briefing.
"There was a multitude of ordnance moving through the Wainwright training area," he said, including a grenade launcher, grenades, small arms and ammunition.
A grass fire ignited about 1km (0.6 miles) away, with the cause currently under investigation, and moved toward the attack range.
"What I would say is there was multiple training activities happening throughout the training area at the time," he said. "Uncommonly strong winds caused the fire to spread rapidly and shift direction towards the range administrative area."
Cannon fire had been heard coming from the base on Saturday before it suddenly stopped, Mayor Pugh told the BBC, noting it's not uncommon to hear cannons being fired there.
News then came through that local emergency services had been deployed to an "all hands on deck" situation.
Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".
The people who were hurt were on the attack range and included reservists and soldiers from the Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, officials said.
In a statement early on Sunday, the Canadian Armed Forces said that "while the incident remains under investigation, at this time, there are no indications that it was the result of any terrorist activity".
Rutland told the briefing: "We do not believe this [incident] to be a result of any oil and gas infrastructure nor any outside interference".
What we know so far about deadly fire at Canadian military base
Wainwright, about 210km (130 miles) east of Edmonton, Alberta's capital, is one of the main bases used by the Canadian military for live-fire training exercises, and it houses troops from Canada and allied countries. About 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers are on site on a typical day.
Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, told broadcaster CBC that the number of patients involved in the incident had "completely overwhelmed" healthcare facilities in Wainwright.
The Royal Alexandra Hospital is in Edmonton, where patients are being transferred. The hospital at first declared a code orange - a disaster-response protocol for a high-casualty incident. That has since been stood down.
Image caption, Wainwright is about 200km (125 miles) from Edmonton, the provincial capital
The provincial health agency said in a statement on Sunday that it deployed 30 units directly into Wainwright, including 22 ground ambulances, six fixed-wing and two rotary wing units.
"It is anticipated that care for patients impacted by this incident will be intensive and will add to existing high demand on acute care in Alberta," it said, adding that patients were being treated at facilities across the province.
STARS, the regional air ambulance service, said aircraft and crews from Edmonton, Saskatoon, and Calgary had been deployed.
Brandon Simmons, who lives in long-term care at the Wainwright Health Centre, told Reuters that when code orange was announced, nurses dropped everything and immediately started grabbing stretchers, gurneys and medical equipment before running to the front entrance.
Ambulances kept coming "throughout the night", he said.
"I heard people screaming inside of those vehicles that will never end up being out of my mind," he recalled, saying it was "like a scene from a war movie".

Image caption, Gleaning Cornwall relies on volunteers to reduce food waste on farms
A gleaning group has saved Â£1m worth of fruit and vegetables that would have been left in field and donated them to food banks.
Gleaning Cornwall relies on volunteers to collect unwanted produce from harvested fields, delivering it to 160 food banks, community larders and kitchens across the South West.
Despite reaching the seven-figure milestone, the group has warned more funding is needed in order to keep up with demand.
Reliance on food banks is increasing and since 2015 the number of known settings providing food aid in Cornwall has risen from 20 to 180, according to Cornwall Council.
Image caption, The gleaning group has saved 460 tonnes of produce since the start of 2020
Gleaning Cornwall started in 2020 and said it had repurposed more than 460 tonnes of produce since then.
But the charity's founder, Holly Whitelaw, warned it was now threatened by economic constraints.
"There is less money around and we need to do more with it," she said. "Our infrastructure urgently needs funding if we are to keep going."
The charity said it fed 11,000 people every week with the stipulation that all its produce must be completely free to recipients.
However, the organisation said the cost of transport, storage and coordination was rising sharply.
It comes at a time when food bank usage is higher than ever with statistics from Cornwall's Trussell Trust showing its food banks distributed more than 35,500 emergency food parcels between April 2024 and March 2025.
A study by Cornwall Council found that 30% of children in the county are living in food poverty.
Whitelaw encouraged people to play their part by reducing the amount of food they wasted at home.
She said: "If we waste food, we waste the substantial energy that went into producing it.
"Utilising what we already have saves money and helps the environment."

On October 19, ahead of the China A-share market open, a dense batch of policy and earnings news landed. China's leadership designated computing power networks as one of the "six networks" in national planning and construction, and the State Council Executive Meeting called for deepening the "AI+" initiative and pushing technology deployment with a focus on the real economy. China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology proposed adding 40 technologies in artificial intelligence, biopharmaceuticals and solar power to the export-restriction list, with temporary registration requirements. The 2026 Financial Street Forum Annual Conference opens the same day, with heads of the People's Bank of China, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange slated to deliver keynote speeches. On earnings, CXMT expects first-three-quarter net profit of 131 billion to 132.5 billion yuan (about $19.6 billion to $19.8 billion), a turnaround from a year-earlier loss, and its chairman proposed a 1 billion to 2 billion yuan buyback. AI supply chain companies including Shengyi Technology, Demingli, Hengtong Optic-Electric and Wellyhigh reported sharp profit increases. Weakness in U.S. and Japanese-South Korean semiconductor stocks may weigh on opening sentiment.

Ahead of the October 19 open, China's A-share market is absorbing a dense flow of policy and earnings information. On one side, China's top leadership issued new directives on computing infrastructure and the "AI+" initiative, while the Financial Street Forum Annual Conference opens in Beijing the same day, with the heads of four financial regulators set to speak collectively. On the other, AI supply chain companies spanning memory, copper-clad laminates and PCBs (printed circuit boards) clustered in disclosing first-three-quarter earnings forecasts, with several posting turnarounds or multi-fold growth. CXMT drew the spotlight with a cumulative profit forecast of more than 130 billion yuan (about $19.5 billion).
On policy, Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and president of China, said during an inspection tour on October 16 in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, that computing power networks are one of the "six networks" in national planning and construction, and that the computing power industry is in a phase of accelerated development with broad prospects. He called for implementing requirements for efficiency, green development and security, emphasizing "computing-power and electricity coordination" and "computing-power and water coordination," building and operating computing center projects well, and actively promoting the development of green computing power. The State Council Executive Meeting held the same day, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, noted that artificial intelligence is a key variable shaping future development and called for using deployment applications to pull technological innovation, deepening and expanding the "AI+" initiative, strengthening supply-demand linkage with a focus on the real economy, advancing pilot-scale validation, and expanding application scenarios so that AI technology translates more effectively into real productivity.
On external technology management, China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology opened a public consultation on revisions to the Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited or Restricted from Export, proposing to add 40 technologies across artificial intelligence, biopharmaceuticals and solar power, and to impose temporary registration management on exports of the relevant technologies. The AI category covers 23 technologies related to large models, intelligent agents, computing clusters and information processing; technologies already in the public domain through open-source release or academic publication would not be covered. The biopharmaceutical category covers five technologies related to cell and gene therapy, small nucleic acid drugs and pathogenic microorganisms, with outbound licensing models that do not involve ownership transfer eligible for facilitation measures such as automatic licensing. The solar category covers 12 technologies related to polysilicon manufacturing, wafer manufacturing and cell manufacturing, along with key core equipment embodying those technologies.
On finance, the 2026 Financial Street Forum Annual Conference runs from October 19 to 22 at Beijing's Financial Street under the theme "Openness, Cooperation, Inclusiveness — Building a New Ecosystem for Global Financial Development," drawing more than 400 guests from over 40 countries and regions. Pan Gongsheng, governor of the People's Bank of China; Ding Xiangqun, head of the National Financial Regulatory Administration; Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission; and Zhu Hexin, head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, will attend and deliver keynote speeches. Separately, the People's Bank of China opened a public consultation on Rules for Bond Issuance Management in the Interbank Bond Market, specifying that issue prices, interest rates and commission fees should be determined on a market basis, and prohibiting conduct that affects fair bond pricing or involves improper transfer of benefits.
On industry regulation, four Chinese ministries — the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the State Administration for Market Regulation — organized a discussion with more than 30 major automakers, requiring them to firmly resist irrational competition, comprehensively strengthen testing and validation, truthfully publicize the usage boundaries and limitations of innovative product designs, refrain from false, exaggerated or misleading advertising, and avoid inducing drivers to neglect safe-driving responsibilities. Next steps include accelerating the revision of relevant standards, continuing supervisory inspections of major automakers and publicly exposing problematic companies. The National Development and Reform Commission, the National Energy Administration and other departments, meanwhile, held a meeting in Taiyuan, Shanxi, on accelerating the resumption and increase of coal mine production to ensure supply, requiring "one mine, one policy" restart plans and pushing temporarily suspended mines to resume operations quickly and reach full capacity as soon as possible.
Earnings are the most concentrated focus ahead of the open. CXMT announced it expects first-three-quarter 2026 revenue of about 265 billion to 270 billion yuan (about $39.7 billion to $40.4 billion), an increase of 232.916 billion to 237.916 billion yuan from a year earlier, and net profit attributable to shareholders of about 131 billion to 132.5 billion yuan (about $19.6 billion to $19.8 billion), compared with a loss of 5.28 billion yuan (about $790.9 million) a year earlier — a swing to profit. The company attributed the results to AI computing demand growth and improving DRAM industry conditions, which left products in short supply and drove sharp price increases. The same day, the board received a letter from Chairman Zhu Yiming proposing a share buyback of 1 billion to 2 billion yuan (about $149.8 million to $299.6 million) through centralized bidding at a price no higher than 150% of the average trading price over the 30 trading days before the board resolution approving the buyback, with repurchased shares intended for employee equity incentives, employee stock ownership plans or reduction of registered capital.
Other companies in the supply chain also posted strong results. Shengyi Technology expects first-three-quarter net profit attributable to shareholders of 6.46 billion to 6.87 billion yuan (about $967.7 million to $1.0 billion), up 164% to 181% year on year, mainly on higher copper-clad laminate sales and increased revenue and gross profit, with its circuit board segment benefiting from the AI computing boom. Demingli expects first-three-quarter revenue of 27.5 billion to 29.5 billion yuan (about $4.1 billion to $4.4 billion), up 312.97% to 343.00%, and net profit attributable to shareholders of 8.65 billion to 8.95 billion yuan (about $1.3 billion), versus a loss of 27.0765 million yuan (about $4.1 million) a year earlier, with enterprise storage revenue and its share of the total rising further. Hengtong Optic-Electric expects first-three-quarter net profit of 5.97 billion to 6.37 billion yuan (about $894.3 million to $954.2 million), up 151.27% to 168.10%.

KeXiang Co. reported third-quarter revenue of 1.85 billion yuan (about $277.1 million), up 100.90%, and net profit attributable to shareholders of 311 million yuan (about $46.6 million), a turnaround from a year-earlier loss. Wellyhigh posted third-quarter revenue of 877 million yuan (about $131.4 million), up 115.24%, and net profit of 138 million yuan (about $20.7 million), up 461.86%; the company said demand for AI server power supplies surged, AC-DC product orders grew rapidly, and AI server power products accounted for about 63% of main business revenue in the period. Tengjing Technology expects third-quarter net profit attributable to shareholders of 44 million to 48 million yuan (about $6.6 million to $7.2 million), up 61.68% to 76.38%, benefiting from global expansion of AI computing infrastructure and sustained order growth for optical test instruments such as passive optical components for high-speed data center optical modules.
On buybacks and capital moves, Cheng Yuhua, an independent director of Montage Technology, proposed a buyback of 3 billion to 5 billion yuan (about $44.9 million to $74.9 million) of A-shares using the company's own funds for an employee stock ownership plan or equity incentives. The chairman of Dawning Information Industry proposed a buyback of 3 billion to 5 billion yuan, the chairman of Hygon Information Technology proposed 5 billion to 8 billion yuan (about $74.9 million to $119.8 million), and the chairman of Shengyi Technology proposed 2 billion to 3 billion yuan (about $30.0 million to $44.9 million). Shenghe Resources plans to transfer 51% stakes in four rare earth smelting and separation subsidiaries, including Leshan Shenghe, to China Rare Earth Group Industrial Development Co., with the targets valued at a combined 3.25 billion to 3.55 billion yuan (about $486.8 million to $531.8 million), corresponding to a transaction price estimated at 1.6575 billion to 1.8105 billion yuan (about $248.3 million to $271.2 million); after the deal, the four companies will no longer be consolidated. Lakala plans to acquire a controlling stake in Guangzhou Gaofu Information Technology Co. through a share issuance and cash payment, with an issue price of 12.88 yuan per share; the target's "Skyee" platform provides cross-border fund settlement services for cross-border e-commerce and foreign trade companies, covering cross-border payments in 175 countries and regions. Lakala's shares will resume trading at the October 19 open.
The external market backdrop is weak. Last Friday, all three major U.S. stock indexes closed lower, with the Dow down 0.34%, the Nasdaq down 2.15% and the S&P 500 down 1.09%; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.83%, its eighth straight session of declines, and the memory concept index plunged 6.28%. Japanese and South Korean markets opened lower today, with South Korea's KOSPI down 3.17%, SK Hynix down more than 4% and Samsung Electronics down more than 3%; Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.77%. Vishal Khanduja, head of fixed income at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, said at the Global Wealth Management Forum 2026 Shanghai Suhewan Conference that global investment in AI data centers is expected to reach about $5 trillion by 2030, but at least 50% of industry participants may fail to generate returns above their cost of capital over the next five years.
On impact, the policy framing of computing power networks and "AI+" echoes the earnings being delivered in concentrated fashion by supply chain companies, which could in the near term reinforce expectations that the upcycle in AI hardware will continue. However, the sustained correction in overseas semiconductor shares and sharp opening declines in Japanese and South Korean memory stocks may weigh on opening sentiment for related China A-share names. If the technology export catalogue revisions take effect, they will directly affect cross-border technology cooperation models in artificial intelligence, biopharmaceuticals and solar power, and companies involved in outbound licensing and open-source routes will need to reassess compliance arrangements. Buyback proposals from several technology leaders alongside their earnings disclosures are also seen as management's statement on valuation and long-term prospects.

items.title: Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks
items.summary: Amid fear of rate hikes and oil prices, investors can look past volatility and track Street analysts' stock picks with strong long-term growth potential.
items.content:
Top analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks
A cyclist rides past the Meta sign outside the headquarters of Facebook parent company Meta Platforms in Mountain View, California, on Nov. 9, 2022.
Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.
Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.
Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.
Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529 . " UNH 's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.
The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.
Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.
Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.
Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%.  See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.
Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction . Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.
Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.
Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.
"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.
While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.
Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%.  See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.
Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology . Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.
After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell 's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370 .
The five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.
While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.
Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.
Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%.  See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

items.title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.
items.content:
Figure caption, Watch: James Waterhouse speaks to looted shop owners on the streets of Paris
French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday.
In a national address from the ÃlysÃ©e Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame."
Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.
Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted".
Police have arrested about 2,400 people, according to France's interior ministry.
The French president said "nothing justifies" the "unbridled" violence seen and said those involved would face justice.
Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.
Figure caption, 'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
On Sunday, looting and clashes with police continued on a smaller scale in parts of the capital and Lyon.
Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people in Paris, according to the AFP news agency, and bottles and rocks were again hurled at police.
Sunday saw cities across the country confront the impact of what developed into one of the worst bouts of disorder in modern French history.
In Limoges, the ornate 19th Century city hall was gutted by a fire started by rioters on Saturday, its clock tower and roof collapsing and the flames took hold.
Image caption, A view of the damage inside Limoges town hall on Sunday morning
Speaking near the ruined building, AnnÃ¨yse said: "This is very upsetting. Harming heritage buildings just because you are angry at the government is selfish, I think. It's hurting everybody."
"It's awful and unbelievable," said another man who gave his name as Gerrard. "We are very sad and I think it will be a long time to put it back as it was before."
Shopkeepers were seen early on Sunday morning picking up large shards of glass in Paris as rubbish trucks cleared up debris on some of the larger streets.
Image caption, Fires were lit and shops looted during smaller scale disorder in Paris on Sunday
Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas.
Macron said local prefects and mayors would draft measures to protect shops and civic buildings.
The president also said there would be "full transparency" over the police response to the demonstrations.
Tear gas and water cannon were turned on crowds over the weekend and riot police were seen hitting people with batons in several places.
France's interior ministry said about 1,000 police officers were injured on Saturday, seven of them seriously.
Image caption, A man tries to extinguish a fire in Paris on Sunday
Student protests which began last month escalated significant on Saturday after they were joined by trade union members and other anti-government groups.
The response from political figures has pointed to France's deep political divisions as the country prepares for an election in April which could see the hard-right pitted against the hard-left.
France's Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez said that while demonstrating was a fundamental right, there were "outrages" committed by "several thousand far-left individuals" who were determined to target public buildings and confront the police.
Later, they were joined by "delinquents who looted and ransacked numerous businesses in several cities in France", he said.
Jean-Luc MÃ©lenchon - leader of the hard-left La France Insoumise party - heavily criticised NuÃ±ez and police chiefs on social media.
He said they had "shown complete incompetence" with their handling of the demonstrations and called them "specialists in organised chaos".
Meanwhile, the leader of the hard-right National Rally party, Marine Le Pen, condemned the "exploitation" of anger "by political forces that encourage violence".
